gen-irish-grover-gf-geist-mono: Chunky and friendly, Irish Grover stands tall with softly shaded strokes, while Geist Mono lays down wire-thin monospace letters with wide gaps. Paragraphs would tick along like typed lines, steady and spacious.
gen-irish-grover-gf-momo-trust-display: Momo Trust Display drifts along with a generous x-height and distant, loosely spaced letters beneath Irish Grover. And a full page of it would move at an unhurried pace, a quiet foil to the sturdy heading.
gen-irish-grover-gf-mukta: Tall, sturdy lowercase gives Irish Grover its big, friendly presence. Irish Grover is best at making words look chunky and playful, while Mukta's plain sans letters, tall-bodied and small, simply get on with the text.
gen-irish-grover-gf-smooch-sans: Sturdy and playful up top: Irish Grover makes a friendly first impression. What stands out is the tension between that softness and Smooch Sans, a tightly packed sans with a high midline.
gen-irish-grover-gf-strait: Strait brings big round bowls and a friendly, contemporary feel. Under the tall, sturdy lines of Irish Grover, those soft curves in the sans text give the eye somewhere gentle to land.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-allerta: Loud, cheerful and poured-looking, Luckiest Guy gets its word in first. Luckiest Guy is best at grabbing attention with solid, uniform-width ink, while Allerta, the sans-serif body, does its best work in wide, loosely tracked lines.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-jaldi: Luckiest Guy shouts in cheerful, poured-looking letters with a high mean line. Jaldi, a sans-serif body with a tall x-height and tightly brushed letters, would carry a page of text with a bit of lean energy.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-matemasie: Loud, open-eyed letters up top: Luckiest Guy hits like a cheer from the back row. But Matemasie, all plain sans with broad gaps between glyphs, quietly does the text work.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-mukta-malar: Cheerful, loud and poured-looking, Luckiest Guy sets the tone fast. Luckiest Guy does best at grabbing a glance with its uniform strokes, while Mukta Malar, the sans-serif body, does best at quiet text with compressed ascenders.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-narnoor: Cheerful and loud, Luckiest Guy keeps its joins thick, while the sans-serif Narnoor tucks short ascenders above big bowls. One shouts from the top while the other settles in underneath.
